source.title: Reverse Substrings Between Each Pair of Parentheses

teaching.hint: When an inner pair closes, what text should the surrounding pair hold?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Nested groups finish in last-opened, first-closed order; each group’s resolved text can be transformed before becoming part of its parent.
solution_outline.approach: Scan left to right, keeping a partial string for each open nesting level. Opening a pair starts a new partial result; closing it reverses its resolved contents and appends them to the parent; letters append to the current level.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each active level stores exactly the resolved text encountered in that pair so far, with all deeper closed groups already transformed and merged.
solution_outline.correctness: Balanced parentheses guarantee every close matches the current deepest group. Reversing that completed group performs the required inner-first step, and induction over closes shows the outer result is correct with all parentheses removed.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n×d) time in the worst case for nesting depth d≤n because characters may be recopied at each outer reversal; O(n) auxiliary space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Reversing text at an opening parenthesis or reversing outer content before inner content changes the specified order.

common_wrong_turns: Reverse an outer group before resolving its children
source_fidelity_notes: Retained a compact nested example to disambiguate inner-first reversal.
